subject.title: fix: block no-auth managed gateway LAN installs

question: Should OpenClaw accept blocking explicit no-auth non-loopback managed Gateway installs during install/refresh before service rewrite?
rationale: The patch is functionally aligned with the runtime security invariant, but it deliberately changes when existing invalid managed-service setups fail and may require operator action during install or update refresh.

options.title: Accept the earlier install block
options.body: Merge the PR as a clearer install-time enforcement of the existing no-auth non-loopback runtime refusal.

options.title: Require fuller managed-service proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted Windows Scheduled Task or equivalent managed-service run before accepting the compatibility change.

options.title: Pause for broader update proof
options.body: Hold this PR until the original update-mutation claim is reproduced, accepting that the narrower managed-install gap remains open.

recommendation.title: Accept the earlier install block
recommendation.body: Merge the PR as a clearer install-time enforcement of the existing no-auth non-loopback runtime refusal.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is both the listed project lead and the strongest local history owner for the Gateway runtime/install safety boundary.
